edition.en: Poems of the Past and the Present (1901), on Project Gutenberg (eBook 3168)
edition.zh: 据古登堡计划电子书 3168 所录《今昔诗集》（1901）

basis.en: First published in December 1900; the author died in 1928.
basis.zh: 1900 年 12 月首次发表；作者卒于 1928 年。

note.en: Dated December 1900 and first printed in the last days of the nineteenth century. Everything in the first half is frost and ending; then an old, thin thrush sings, and Hardy, who was not given to optimism, admits that the bird may know of some hope he does not. It is a winter poem for a cold library, and its light is small but real.
note.zh: 诗末署“1900 年 12 月”，在十九世纪的最后几天首次付印。前半首全是霜冻与终结；然后一只又老又瘦的画眉唱起来，一向不轻言乐观的哈代承认：这只鸟也许知道某种他不知道的希望。这是一首写给冷冻图书馆的冬天的诗，它的光很小，却是真的。

excerpt.orig:
Some blessed Hope, whereof he knew
And I was unaware.
excerpt.en:
Some blessed Hope, whereof he knew
And I was unaware.
excerpt.zh:
某种神圣的希望，他知道，
而我却不知道。
